title: Space junk
paragraphs: Many of us ponder what lies in outer space. When we look up at the night sky, we see stars, the twinkle of a moving satellite and occasionally a distant planet. But one thing we don’t see is the millions of pieces of junk filling up space. It’s this debris that’s causing problems for the existing technology that’s up there and which we rely on.

The amount of space junk is increasing. Over the last few decades, satellites and rockets have been launched into space, littering the cosmos as they go. It’s estimated there are now millions of discarded pieces of metal and other materials in orbit – everything from old rocket segments to accidentally dropped astronaut tools, and even flecks of paint. The fear is that if we don’t start taking this litter out of the sky soon, it will become a significant threat to active satellites. Nobu Okada, Chief Executive of Astroscale – a company working on ways to clean up space junk – says hitting “even a small paint fleck… has enough power to blow up other satellites.”

Several ideas are being looked at to capture the debris floating around in space. In 2018, the RemoveDebris spacecraft carried out various experiments, including testing a net that could snare a satellite and firing a harpoon at a target in orbit to try to catch it.

This year the UK Space Agency is helping to fund new approaches to tracking satellites and debris in space. Jacob Geer from UKSA told the BBC: “Space surveillance and tracking is one of the key things we can do to keep safe those satellites we rely on now, and to make sure certain orbits don’t become inaccessible for future generations because there’s too much debris in them.”

It’s clear that a solution is needed so a celestial deep clean can take place. But looking to the future, like any litter problem, we need to look at ways of creating less – and that shouldn’t be the stuff of science fiction.

vocabulary.entry: ponder /ˈpɒndə/ v. 思索；深思
vocabulary.example: She paused to ponder the meaning of his words.
vocabulary.translation: 她停下来思索他话语中的含义。

vocabulary.entry: outer space /ˈaʊtə speɪs/ n. 外太空
vocabulary.example: The rocket will travel through outer space to Mars.
vocabulary.translation: 这枚火箭将穿越外太空飞往火星。

vocabulary.entry: twinkle /ˈtwɪŋkl/ n. 闪烁的光点
vocabulary.example: We saw the twinkle of distant city lights.
vocabulary.translation: 我们看到了远处城市灯光的闪烁。

vocabulary.entry: satellite /ˈsætəlaɪt/ n. 卫星
vocabulary.example: The satellite sends back images of the Earth every day.
vocabulary.translation: 这颗卫星每天发回地球的图像。

vocabulary.entry: distant planet /ˈdɪstənt ˈplænɪt/ n. 遥远的行星
vocabulary.example: Astronomers have discovered a new distant planet in the galaxy.
vocabulary.translation: 天文学家在银河系中发现了一颗新的遥远行星。

vocabulary.entry: space junk /speɪs dʒʌŋk/ n. 太空垃圾
vocabulary.example: Space junk poses a threat to spacecraft in orbit.
vocabulary.translation: 太空垃圾对轨道上的航天器构成威胁。

vocabulary.entry: debris /ˈdebriː/ n. 碎片；残骸
vocabulary.example: The storm left a lot of debris on the streets.
vocabulary.translation: 暴风雨过后街上满是残骸。

vocabulary.entry: existing technology /ɪɡˈzɪstɪŋ tekˈnɒlədʒi/ n. 现有技术
vocabulary.example: We need to upgrade the existing technology to improve efficiency.
vocabulary.translation: 我们需要升级现有技术来提高效率。

vocabulary.entry: litter /ˈlɪtə/ v. 使散落垃圾；弄乱
vocabulary.example: Tourists are warned not to litter the countryside.
vocabulary.translation: 游客被提醒不要在乡间乱扔垃圾。

vocabulary.entry: cosmos /ˈkɒzmɒs/ n. 宇宙
vocabulary.example: The astronomer devoted his life to exploring the cosmos.
vocabulary.translation: 这位天文学家毕生致力于探索宇宙。

vocabulary.entry: discarded /dɪˈskɑːdɪd/ adj. 被废弃的
vocabulary.example: They found some discarded furniture by the roadside.
vocabulary.translation: 他们在路边发现了一些被丢弃的家具。

vocabulary.entry: orbit /ˈɔːbɪt/ n. （天体等的）运行轨道
vocabulary.example: The moon moves in an orbit around the Earth.
vocabulary.translation: 月球沿着围绕地球的轨道运行。

vocabulary.entry: rocket segment /ˈrɒkɪt ˈseɡmənt/ n. 火箭箭体
vocabulary.example: The rocket segment fell into the ocean after launch.
vocabulary.translation: 火箭箭体发射后坠入了海洋。

vocabulary.entry: astronaut tool /ˈæstrənɔːt tuːl/ n. 宇航员工具
vocabulary.example: The astronaut tool was lost during a spacewalk.
vocabulary.translation: 这件宇航员工具在太空行走时遗失了。

vocabulary.entry: fleck of paint /flek ɒv peɪnt/ n. 油漆颗粒
vocabulary.example: A tiny fleck of paint was found on the victim's clothes.
vocabulary.translation: 在受害者的衣服上发现了一小粒油漆。

vocabulary.entry: significant threat /sɪɡˈnɪfɪkənt θret/ n. 严重威胁
vocabulary.example: Pollution is a significant threat to marine life.
vocabulary.translation: 污染对海洋生物构成严重威胁。

vocabulary.entry: active satellite /ˈæktɪv ˈsætəlaɪt/ n. 在轨运行卫星
vocabulary.example: The active satellite is used for global communication.
vocabulary.translation: 这颗在轨运行卫星用于全球通信。

vocabulary.entry: capture /ˈkæptʃə/ v. 捕获；俘获
vocabulary.example: The police managed to capture the escaped prisoner.
vocabulary.translation: 警方成功捕获了越狱的囚犯。

vocabulary.entry: snare /sneə/ v. 用网捕捉
vocabulary.example: The fishermen used a net to snare the fish.
vocabulary.translation: 渔民们用网捕鱼。

vocabulary.entry: harpoon /hɑːˈpuːn/ n. 鱼叉
vocabulary.example: The hunter threw a harpoon at the whale.
vocabulary.translation: 猎人向鲸鱼投掷了鱼叉。

vocabulary.entry: space surveillance /speɪs səˈveɪləns/ n. 太空监测
vocabulary.example: Space surveillance systems track objects in orbit.
vocabulary.translation: 太空监测系统追踪轨道上的物体。

vocabulary.entry: inaccessible /ˌɪnækˈsesəbl/ adj. 无法进入的；难以企及的
vocabulary.example: The ancient temple is located in an inaccessible mountain area.
vocabulary.translation: 这座古庙位于一个难以进入的山区。

sentences.english: Many of us ponder what lies in outer space.
sentences.chinese: 我们很多人都会思索外太空究竟存在着什么。

sentences.english: When we look up at the night sky, we see stars, the twinkle of a moving satellite and occasionally a distant planet.
sentences.chinese: 当我们仰望夜空时，能看到繁星、移动卫星闪烁的光点，偶尔还能瞥见遥远的行星。

sentences.english: But one thing we don’t see is the millions of pieces of junk filling up space.
sentences.chinese: 但有一样东西我们是看不到的，那就是充斥在太空中的数百万块垃圾。

sentences.english: It’s this debris that’s causing problems for the existing technology that’s up there and which we rely on.
sentences.chinese: 正是这些太空碎片，给我们目前在轨运行且赖以生存的技术设备带来了麻烦。

sentences.english: The amount of space junk is increasing.
sentences.chinese: 太空垃圾的数量正在不断增加。

sentences.english: Over the last few decades, satellites and rockets have been launched into space, littering the cosmos as they go.
sentences.chinese: 在过去几十年里，人类向太空发射了大量卫星和火箭，这些设备在升空过程中也给宇宙留下了遍地狼藉。

sentences.english: It’s estimated there are now millions of discarded pieces of metal and other materials in orbit – everything from old rocket segments to accidentally dropped astronaut tools, and even flecks of paint.
sentences.chinese: 据估计，如今轨道上漂浮着数百万块废弃的金属及其他材料碎片，比如老旧的火箭箭体，到宇航员不慎掉落的工具，甚至还有微小的油漆颗粒。

sentences.english: The fear is that if we don’t start taking this litter out of the sky soon, it will become a significant threat to active satellites.
sentences.chinese: 人们担心，如果不尽快清理这些太空垃圾，它们将会对在轨运行的卫星构成严重威胁。

sentences.english: Nobu Okada, Chief Executive of Astroscale – a company working on ways to clean up space junk – says hitting “even a small paint fleck… has enough power to blow up other satellites.”
sentences.chinese: 致力于研发太空垃圾清理技术的星舰公司首席执行官冈田伸表示，哪怕是一小块油漆颗粒，一旦发生撞击，其产生的威力也足以摧毁其他卫星。

sentences.english: Several ideas are being looked at to capture the debris floating around in space.
sentences.chinese: 目前人们正在研究多种方案，用于捕获漂浮在太空中的碎片。

sentences.english: In 2018, the RemoveDebris spacecraft carried out various experiments, including testing a net that could snare a satellite and firing a harpoon at a target in orbit to try to catch it.
sentences.chinese: 2018年，“太空清理”号航天器开展了多项实验，其中包括测试一种可捕获卫星的网，以及向轨道目标发射鱼叉以尝试捕捉碎片。

sentences.english: This year the UK Space Agency is helping to fund new approaches to tracking satellites and debris in space.
sentences.chinese: 今年，英国航天局出资支持了多项追踪在轨卫星与太空碎片的新方案研究。

sentences.english: Jacob Geer from UKSA told the BBC: “Space surveillance and tracking is one of the key things we can do to keep safe those satellites we rely on now, and to make sure certain orbits don’t become inaccessible for future generations because there’s too much debris in them.”
sentences.chinese: 英国航天局的雅各布·吉尔在接受BBC采访时表示：“太空监测与追踪是我们目前能采取的关键措施之一，既能保护我们当下依赖的卫星安全运行，也能避免部分轨道因碎片过多而变得无法使用，从而给后代留下可用的太空轨道资源。”

sentences.english: It’s clear that a solution is needed so a celestial deep clean can take place.
sentences.chinese: 显然，我们亟需找到解决方案，来开展一场太空大扫除。

sentences.english: But looking to the future, like any litter problem, we need to look at ways of creating less – and that shouldn’t be the stuff of science fiction.
sentences.chinese: 而放眼未来，和处理任何垃圾问题的思路一样，我们需要想方设法减少太空垃圾的产生——这绝非什么科幻情节，而是切实可行的举措。
